questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How scientists predict wildfires
Why Los Angeles has so many fires
How to build homes that survive floods
How climate change can harm mental health, and how communities help
questions.why: They discuss how climate change affects mental health and how people can protect it.

questions.q: Do Neil and Beth agree that natural disasters can be stressful?
options: Yes, they both agree
No, Beth thinks they are rarely stressful
Only Neil thinks so
They don't discuss it
questions.why: Neil says they can be stressful and asks Beth, who answers, 'Yeah, definitely.'

questions.q: What has Professor Jyoti Mishra found about climate trauma?
options: It mainly affects children
It usually disappears after a few weeks without any help
It affects whole communities, not just individuals
It is less serious than other kinds of trauma
questions.why: She says it's 'a community-wide trauma which really requires community-wide healing'.

questions.q: According to Jyoti, which people are usually more resilient?
options: People who move to a new city
People with family support and strong community connections
People who live alone
People who have already lived through many different disasters
questions.why: She says people with positive family support and meaningful community connection are more resilient.

questions.q: What does host Graihagh Jackson find particularly interesting?
options: That the fires were caused by humans
That trauma after a disaster can be treated quickly with medicine
That both the harm and the solution involve the whole community
That most people recover alone
questions.why: She is struck that whole communities are affected and the solution is about how the community rebuilds.

questions.q: What happened to Brad Sherwood in 2017?
options: He lost his job because of a flood
He started a company that builds new houses for families after floods
He moved to Los Angeles
He survived a wildfire, but his neighbourhood was destroyed
questions.why: He survived the Tubbs fire, but when he returned home his neighbourhood was destroyed.

questions.q: What does Brad suggest about his community since the fire?
options: It is now stronger and is building a new plaza together
Most people have moved away
It was never close before the fire
People are still far too upset to work together on anything new
questions.why: He says they're building a new community plaza and are now 'so much stronger and resilient'.

questions.q: How does Beth feel about Brad's story?
options: She thinks it is very sad
She finds it quite inspiring
She doesn't believe it
She thinks he was just very lucky
questions.why: Beth says it's 'quite inspiring' to hear how Brad stayed resilient.
